analysis: The supplied changes are documentation only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (new 'Deadline admission rates' section at head lines 457-482, a Code-map row at line 536, plus a refreshed Super/memory narrative) and docs/architecture/inference.md (out-of-order observation freshness, TTFT admission estimator corrections, Deadlines code-map row). No executable code, wire contract, key handling, attestation, authorization or encryption path changes. Checked against the threat model: nothing touches A-001/A-003 plaintext or key custody, the TB-002 websocket, TB-011 App Attest authorization (T-053/T-054), or the T-041 prefix-cache at-rest posture (HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, KEK purge). The docs state capacity wire fields and the platform memory contract are unchanged, and that deadline admission is a time check which still passes slot and process byte admission. Documentation says DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 restores the old estimators; this is a local operator env knob and does not alter trust boundaries. The described behaviors (an anchor floor on isolated prefill rate, evidence older than 30 minutes treated as absent, decode charged per step, freshness anchored to the newest observation) affect only provider-local admission and DoS/availability heuristics. Admitting a request slightly more optimistically could raise deadline misses, but this is performance policy, not a confidentiality or authorization regression, and the underlying Swift sources (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, EngineV2Bridge) were not supplied, so those claims cannot be verified here. Remaining integration question: whether the code changes accompanying these docs preserve the stated unchanged memory-admission guarantees; they are outside this batch. Inference.md unit 0 carried metadata only, with the patch in unit 1.
